utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner and Ann Sutherland assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager, good morning Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, I'm Milan Trbojevic, attorney at law, together with me is lead counsel, Mr. John Ackerman and Marela Jevtovic our legal assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. Shall we go -- anything before we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour there is one matter I want to raise having yesterday but at the end of the whole session having only had a chance yesterday to read Your Honour's ruling on the disclosure of Rule 68 material, there are a couple of factual mistakes which I ought to correct but I'll do that if I may like Mr. Ackerman yesterday if we adjourn at -- adjourn -- stop the witness at about 25 to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And from your part? Okay? So Madam Registrar, could we go into closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's just in relation to Your Honour's ruling which as I say I only had a chance to read yesterday, of the 30th of October in relation to Mr. Ackerman's motion. Your Honours, in paragraph 11, stated that we had failed to disclose the Kondic Rule 68 material because it had only come up in a search we were doing on Prijedor material. And it refers to the discussion in the unofficial transcript as a footnote. Your Honour, all I want to say is this: In fact I understand why whoever was trying to summarise this made that error but I never said that. What I was saying was that we had unfortunately delayed in the disclosure and I accepted full responsibility for it because the investigator who was present had been taken off that disclosure to deal with the Prijedor Rule 68 searches that were going but it wasn't that it came up in that. We knew it was there. It just fell through the cracks. But I felt it wasn't right to take credit for something that wasn't actually right or something that I didn't say. That's the first thing. Your Honour, the references to the transcript page numbers are right but if one reads it you'll see that's not what I said. And secondly, Your Honour, I think again there was a lot of discussion and I was referring to a table. Your Honours were under the impression that there were only two additional interviews which had not had Rule 68 disclosed. That is in fact incorrect. And I think again there was an elision. Your Honour I referred to a number of Prijedor interviews that had been conducted in connection with the Stakic case and then I referred separately to what I described as confidential, as which I said there were a couple. In actual fact, we having now, and we are more or less completing the exercise to comply with Your Honour's order. There are a further, we worked this out yesterday -- where is my note? There were five people interviewed in connection with the Stakic case, of which disclosure I think has already been -- there is just one more to come but four out of the five have already been disclosed and then there were altogether, including interviews conducted with persons in respect of the military prosecutions, but there were a total of 12 altogether. So those -- there were 12 people who the Defence had not had anything from but it's been disclosed at the moment, but again, I didn't want Your Honours to feel in some way you were being misled. I'm afraid it was partly the way matters developed during the course of that hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any comments from your part, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, she's absolutely correct with regard to the first part. That's exactly what she said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Second part, the more the better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The important thing is that the whole matter is being taken care of. That's most important. Thank you for clarifying certain points, Ms. Korner. So I think we can rise. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour I just have a sort of nagging sense in the back of my mind that there is a motion or two outstanding, the Prosecutor has filed, that I have not responded to, and I would like to go home and check that and have your leave to file a response in the event that I might be a day or two late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I also would like you to address your attention to some motions that have been filed by Defence counsel for General Talic, some of which I am positive have -- are not to be discussed in this trial or by this Trial Chamber or decided by this Trial Chamber, but there is one or two that probably need to be discussed and decided upon by this Trial Chamber. So I would like you, if you have been served, the Prosecution has filed responses to them. I don't know whether you have been served with any of these as Defence counsel in the Brdjanin case. At least there is one of which I'm positive that you must have been served with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There is one that involves certain evidence -- to prohibit certain evidence in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is one which requests this Trial Chamber to authorise the release to General Talic of the basically the proceedings in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as we say in Texas, I don't have a dog in either one of those fights so I really don't plan to answer either one of them unless you actually ask me too. I don't really have an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm just addressing you since you mentioned pending motions I'm addressing you to these in case you require some sort of debate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think the only one that was filed within this constituted Trial Chamber is the one about the release of material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honours have seen our response and we have nothing further to add. I think outstanding is our application under Rule 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is another one, Ms. Korner, which is a little bit of an anomalous kind of request, in the sense that it is filed in Talic's case but asking that Trial Chamber to order this Trial Chamber not to allow certain questions or allow certain evidence to be brought forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's already been dealt with in this Trial Chamber as a result of the application which I think we said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But any way, please do whatever you have that you need to be debated here, do let us know and we'll find the time. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is there any update on the progress on a ruling regarding Ms. Maglov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We talked about it earlier on today. We are dealing with it but, there is an order of priority and -- I'm being told also judicial notice that's an important one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's the one that I was kind of thinking about in the back of my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I will answer that probably today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Ms. Maglov decision we will come down with when we really find the time to give a well-reasoned decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me just say this to give you some sense that there might be a matter of urgency with regard to. There is nobody that has more knowledge of the documents in this case up until the time she left the case, than she does, and if she is to be cleared of everything, then I might very well want to have her as a legal assistant or something, because she would be great assistance to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is also the other possibility, Mr. Ackerman, and I don't think that possibility would help you much. So let us take our time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Take all the time you want, Your Honour. I just wanted to make sure that you understood that part of it. I certainly see the other side of it too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour the last thing Your Honour indicated you wanted a meeting and I don't think you indicated which day or what time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going -- in fact, I was going to end with this -- end up with this. I was going to suggest tomorrow for a meeting during one of the breaks we will have a half an hour break, either the first one or the second one, and we will meet in my Chambers together with Mr. Rohde and sort out the problem of the hours involved in -- or needed for the proper preparation of this case following the disclosure of tapes and printed material.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We probably also would need to get Ms. Monica Martinez involved since she is taking over that position from Mr. Rohde.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Mr. Rohde has already advised me on that and so I'm perfectly aware of it. I'm also informed that there have been informal consultations between you and Mr. Rohde already and that Mr. Rohde has indicated to you what he would be prepared to concede. In any case, I don't think we can even think of -- conceive of a meeting, of such meeting, leaving out Mr. Rohde. Ms. Martinez of course will be present too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Please don't hear me as having said that we should leave Mr. Rohde out. He should definitely be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, so Ms. Chuqing could you inquire about the availability of them for tomorrow. If it's not convenient for them, any of the two normal breaks, that is the one at 10.30 and the other one at 12.30 then if they have other suggestions we could adjust the time of our sitting accordingly and have a break when it's convenient for them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: One other brief thing I've been told that we are meeting Monday morning at 9.00 and that that's our schedule for Monday and in view of that I want to make -- to schedule some important matters for Monday afternoon. If that's the way it's going to be, please don't change it because what I want to do Monday afternoon is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Monday we are meeting in the morning, yes, 11 of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Tuesday we are moving to court II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tuesday we are moving to Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Also in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's in the afternoon, Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's in the afternoon is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we can move it in the morning then it will be much better because I'm flying back home on that day. So we could actually move the sitting to the morning, it will be better.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, because the rate we are going I don't think we are going to get beyond there witness this week. And the witness 7.45 who is actually arriving today but to listen to his tapes. But if possible, we ought to be able to complete in those two days so he doesn't have to hang around or be sent back because that's what happened in Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We will definitely not complete his cross-examination in that time. We won't even get close. We might get a direct done but cross-examination is going to be, who knows, five days? I don't know, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks. Ms. Chuqing? So we'll meet tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.51 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
